detail: lt(user_id, vi, en, zh, **kwargs) resolves via direct dict indexing `{"vi": vi, "en": en, "zh": zh}[get_user_lang(user_id)]` with no .get()/fallback. It is only crash-safe today because normalize_lang() is hard-pinned to always return one of vi/en/zh. Adding a 4th supported language via SUPPORTED_LANGS/_LANG_ALIASES without ALSO updating every lt() call site (333 occurrences across 30 files) and every similar raw dict-literal ({'vi':..,'en':..,'zh':..}[get_user_lang(...)]) in store_callback.py, payment_generation.py, priority_and_text.py, store_menu.py, ui_and_email.py would cause an immediate KeyError/500 for any user whose language resolves to the new code.
evidence: app/utils/i18n.py:324-326: `def lt(user_id, vi: str, en: str, zh: str, **kwargs) -> str:` / `text = {"vi": vi, "en": en, "zh": zh}[get_user_lang(user_id)]`

key: test coverage gap for lt()-based strings
detail: Key-parity enforcement (test_all_languages_have_the_same_translation_keys) only covers the STRINGS dict (56 keys). The other translation mechanism used throughout the codebase -- lt(user_id, vi, en, zh) with ~333 call sites across 30 files, plus ~10 ad-hoc per-locale dict literals in 6 files -- has no automated check that all three language arguments are present/non-placeholder/distinct. A new lt() call added with a missing or copy-pasted-wrong-language string would not fail any existing test.
evidence: tests/test_i18n.py:32-35 `def test_all_languages_have_the_same_translation_keys(): expected = set(i18n.STRINGS[i18n.DEFAULT_LANG]); for lang in i18n.SUPPORTED_LANGS: assert set(i18n.STRINGS[lang]) == expected` -- scope is STRINGS only, confirmed by zero references to `lt(` anywhere in the three test files.
